st: Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C) and grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Tear the bread into a bowl and pour over [[0.5 cup]] of the milk. Let it soak for 5 minutes, then squeeze it out, saving the milk.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat and cook the onions for 6 minutes until soft and golden. Stir in the garlic, curry powder and turmeric for 1 minute.
Add the ground beef and break it up with a spoon. Cook for 8 minutes until no pink remains.
Stir in the squeezed bread, jam, vinegar, raisins, salt and pepper. Cook for 3 minutes more, then stir in [[1 egg]] to bind it.
Press the meat into the baking dish and smooth the top. Tuck in 2 of the bay leaves.
Whisk the remaining [[2 eggs]] with the remaining [[1 cup]] milk and the saved soaking milk. Pour this evenly over the meat.
Lay the remaining 2 bay leaves on top and scatter the almonds over if using.
Bake for 35 minutes until the custard is set and golden on top.
Let it stand for 10 minutes, then cut into squares. Serve with yellow rice, chutney and sliced banana.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onions for 8 minutes until deep golden.
Add the garlic, ginger and curry powder. Stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and salt and cook for 5 minutes until they break down into a thick paste.
Add the chicken and stir to coat in the spice paste. Cook for 5 minutes.
Pour in the water and bring to a simmer. Cover and cook for 20 minutes.
Add the potatoes and simmer for 20 minutes more until they are tender and the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C). The sauce should be thick.
Cut each loaf in half crosswise. Pull out the soft middle of each half, leaving a sturdy shell about 1 inch thick. Keep the pulled bread for the side.
Stir the cilantro into the curry. Spoon the hot curry into the bread shells, letting it spill over.
Top each with a bread lid or the scooped-out bread and serve right away, eaten with your hands.
Rinse the sausage casings in cool water and soak them for 30 minutes. Run water through them to flush the insides.
Chill the meat chunks in the freezer for 20 minutes until firm but not frozen.
Toast the coriander seeds in a dry pan for 2 minutes, then grind them. Mix with the cloves, nutmeg, pepper, allspice and salt.
Grind the beef and pork together through a meat grinder with a coarse plate, or pulse in a food processor in small batches until coarsely chopped.
Mix the spices and vinegar into the meat with your hands for 2 minutes until the mixture feels sticky.
Fry a spoonful of the meat in a pan until cooked, taste it and add more salt if needed.
Slide a casing onto a sausage stuffer or piping tube and fill it, without packing too tight. Coil the sausage into one long spiral.
Rest the sausage in the fridge for 1 hour so the flavors blend.
Heat a grill or skillet over medium heat with the oil. Cook the coil for 25 minutes, turning it once, until browned and the center reaches 160°F (71°C).
Cut into portions and serve with pap, chakalaka or in a roll.
Heat the oil in a large heavy pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown the beef in two batches for 8 minutes each and set aside.
Lower the heat. Cook the onions in the same pot for 6 minutes until soft, then stir in the garlic for 1 minute.
Return the beef to the pot with the tomatoes, stock, Worcestershire sauce, bay leaves, thyme, salt and pepper.
Cover and simmer on low for 1 hour. Do not stir from here on, so the layers stay neat.
Lay the carrots over the meat, then the potatoes, then the butternut squash. Do not stir.
Cover and cook on low for 60 minutes more until the meat and vegetables are tender.
Check the liquid halfway. If it looks dry, add a splash of water around the edge.
Rest for 10 minutes off the heat, then serve straight from the pot with rice, bread or pap.
Heat the oil in a large pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, ginger, chili and curry powder. Stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the bell peppers and carrots and cook for 6 minutes, stirring now and then.
Stir in the tomatoes and tomato paste and cook for 5 minutes until they break down.
Add the baked beans with their sauce and the salt.
Simmer on low heat for 10 minutes until thick and glossy.
Taste and add more salt or chili if you like. Serve warm or cold with pap, bread or grilled meat.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the tomatoes, sugar, [[0.5 tsp]] of the salt and the pepper. Simmer for 12 minutes until saucy, then keep warm.
In a heavy pot, bring [[3 cups]] of the water and the remaining [[0.5 tsp]] salt to a boil.
Mix [[0.5 cup]] of the cornmeal with the remaining [[1 cup]] cold water to make a smooth paste.
Whisk the paste into the boiling water and cook for 3 minutes, stirring, until it thickens.
Pour in the rest of the cornmeal slowly in a steady stream, stirring hard so no lumps form.
Lower the heat, cover and cook for 15 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes, until it is thick and pulls from the pot.
Stir in the milk and [[1 tbsp]] of the butter until creamy.
Spoon the pap into bowls, make a small dip in each and add the remaining [[1 tbsp]] butter. Serve with the tomato and onion relish.
Cut the beef along the grain into strips about 1 inch thick and 8 inches long. Pat them dry.
Toast the coriander seeds in a dry pan for 2 minutes, then crush them coarsely with a mortar or the back of a pan.
Mix the salt, sugar, pepper, crushed coriander and baking soda in a bowl.
Lay the meat strips in a dish and pour over the vinegar, turning to coat all sides.
Rub the spice mix all over each strip and press it in. Cover and chill for 2 hours, turning once.
Heat the oven to its lowest setting, about 170°F (75°C), and set a rack over a baking tray.
Pat the strips lightly dry with a paper towel. Hang them from the rack with skewers, or lay them on the rack with space between each.
Dry in the oven with the door propped open with a wooden spoon for 5 to 6 hours until firm outside and still slightly soft inside.
Cool completely, slice thinly against the grain and store in the fridge in a paper bag for up to 2 weeks.
Mix the flour, sugar, yeast and salt in a large bowl. Pour in the warm water and mix into a soft, sticky dough.
Knead for 8 minutes on a floured surface until smooth. Place in an oiled bowl, cover and let rise for 1 hour until doubled.
Meanwhile, heat [[1 tbsp]] of the oil in a pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes, then add the garlic and curry powder for 1 minute.
Add the beef and cook for 10 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it reaches 160°F (71°C). Stir in the tomato paste and a splash of water and simmer for 5 minutes. Keep warm.
Divide the risen dough into 8 balls and flatten each slightly. Let them rest for 15 minutes.
Heat the remaining oil in a deep, heavy pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry 2 or 3 balls at a time for about 4 minutes, turning once, until deep golden and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels. Cut each open and fill with the curried mince, or fill with jam instead.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat. Brown the lamb in batches for about 10 minutes total and set aside.
Lower the heat. Cook the onions in the same pot for 8 minutes until soft and golden, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Return the lamb to the pot. Add the tomatoes, cinnamon, cloves, bay leaves, sugar, salt, pepper and water.
Bring to a simmer, cover and cook on low for 1 hour 15 minutes, stirring now and then.
Add the potatoes, pushing them into the sauce. Cover and cook for 30 minutes until the potatoes and lamb are tender.
Uncover, remove the cinnamon, cloves and bay leaves, and simmer for 10 minutes to thicken the sauce.
Taste and add salt. Serve over rice.
Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C) and grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Beat the eggs and [[0.75 cup]] sugar for 3 minutes until pale and thick. Beat in the softened butter and jam.
Stir the baking soda into the vinegar and add it to the egg mixture.
Fold in the flour and salt, alternating with the [[0.5 cup]] milk, until just smooth.
Pour the batter into the dish and bake for 35 minutes until deep golden and a skewer comes out clean.
While it bakes, warm the cream, [[0.5 cup]] butter, [[0.5 cup]] sugar, [[0.5 cup]] milk and the hot water in a pot, stirring until the butter melts and the sugar dissolves. Do not boil.
As soon as the pudding comes out, prick it all over with a skewer.
Pour the hot sauce slowly over the hot pudding and let it soak in for 15 minutes.
Serve warm with custard or ice cream.
Make the syrup first. Stir the sugar, water, cream of tartar, ginger and cinnamon stick in a pot over medium heat until the sugar dissolves.
Boil for 8 minutes without stirring, then add the lemon juice, cool and chill in a bowl for at least 3 hours until icy cold.
Mix the flour, baking powder and salt. Rub in the butter with your fingertips until crumbly.
Beat the egg with the milk and stir into the flour to form a soft dough. Knead briefly, then cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Roll the dough about 1/4 inch thick and cut into strips about 1 inch wide and 3 inches long.
Cut each strip into three parts, leaving one end attached, and braid them. Pinch the ends to seal.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the braids a few at a time for about 2 minutes per side until golden brown.
Lift out with a slotted spoon and drop right away into the cold syrup. Turn and soak for 1 minute.
Drain on a rack and serve cold.

ing: separated, plus 1 yolk for the crust
st: Mix [[1.5 cups]] of the flour, the baking powder, salt and [[0.25 cup]] of the sugar. Rub in [[0.25 cup]] of the butter until crumbly.
Stir in 1 egg yolk and the cold water to form a dough. Chill for 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Press the dough into a 9-inch pie dish and prick the base with a fork.
Bake the crust for 12 minutes until pale gold and set.
Heat the milk and cinnamon stick in a pot over medium heat until it just starts to steam.
Whisk the cornstarch, the remaining [[0.25 cup]] flour and [[0.5 cup]] sugar with 2 egg yolks in a bowl. Slowly whisk in some hot milk, then pour it all back into the pot.
Stir over medium heat for 5 minutes until thick. Remove the cinnamon stick and stir in the remaining [[0.25 cup]] butter and the vanilla.
Whisk the 3 egg whites to soft peaks and fold them gently into the custard.
Pour into the baked crust and bake for 25 minutes until just set with a slight wobble.
Dust with the ground cinnamon and cool before slicing. Serve at room temperature or chilled.
Heat the oven to 350°F and grease a standard 12-hole muffin tin. Rub [[0.5 cup]] cold butter into [[1.5 cups]] flour, [[0.5 tsp]] baking powder and [[0.25 cup]] sugar until crumbly.
Mix in the 3 egg yolks to form a firm dough, adding 1 tablespoon cold water if dry. Chill 15 minutes.
Roll the dough 0.125 inch thick and cut 12 rounds of 3 inches. Press one into each cup.
Spoon about 2 teaspoons apricot jam into each shell. Fill only halfway so the jam does not overflow.
Whip 2 egg whites to stiff peaks, then gradually beat in [[0.5 cup]] sugar until glossy. Fold in [[1 cup]] coconut.
Spoon the coconut meringue over the jam, covering the pastry edges. Bake 20 minutes until golden and the meringue is set.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then lift out onto a rack.
nt: Best swap: raspberry or peach jam for the apricot jam, same amount, and cocoa-free sweetened coconut works if you cut the sugar by 2 tbsp.

ing: cut into chunks, plus 1 sliced for sauce
st: Sauté the sliced onion in [[2 tbsp]] oil over medium heat for 8 minutes until soft. Stir in the garlic, [[2 tbsp]] curry powder and bay leaves for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add [[0.25 cup]] vinegar, [[2 tbsp]] brown sugar, [[3 tbsp]] jam and a pinch of salt. Simmer 5 minutes, then cool completely. The marinade must be cold before it touches raw meat.
Pour the cooled marinade over the lamb cubes. Cover and refrigerate at least 4 hours, ideally overnight, turning once.
Thread lamb, onion chunks and apricot halves alternately onto skewers, finishing each with an apricot. Soak wooden skewers first.
Light coals and let them burn to white ash with medium heat. Grill the sosaties 12 to 15 minutes, turning every 3 minutes and basting with leftover marinade for the first 8 minutes only.
Cook until charred and the lamb reads 145°F inside. Rest 5 minutes and serve with yellow rice or pap.
nt: Grilled over medium braai coals with a sweet-sour baste
Best swap: bake on a rack at 450°F for 18 minutes, turning once. Use chicken thighs or pork shoulder for lamb leg.
